title: A way out for readers above the band
statement: Give learners who already read well above a course's band a test-out or measure-only path, instead of holding them on material they have outgrown.
example: In one grade, 102 of 325 certified readers (31%) worked two to four grades above the course's band.
detail: A deepening analysis of a second-grade reading cohort found 102 of 325 certified readers (31%) working two to four grades above the 420–650L band the course tops out at, 64 of them at about a sixth-grade frontier (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g2-reading/analysis/g2-deepening-addendum.md`, lines 36-38). It named two options: an explicit accelerate-out or test-out path, or accepting that the top band's value is coverage and measurement, not instruction (the same file, lines 43-45). A dropout analysis of the same grade found completion falling as starting ability rose, 32% of the highest scorers doing substantial work against 49–56% in the low and middle bands, and read it as boredom rather than frustration (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g2-reading/analysis/dropout-4-who.md`, lines 19 and 79).
against: The highest-scoring group overlaps older learners placed below their level for remediation, so age and placement may explain part of the gradient (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g2-reading/analysis/dropout-4-who.md`, line 79).

evidence.quote: So **102 of 325 certified G2 readers (31%) work two-to-four grades above the 420–650L band this course tops out at.**
**The 64 students at the 90th+ percentile are reading at a ~6.6-grade instructional frontier — sixth-grade text, in second grade.**

(a) an explicit accelerate-out / test-out path for the top band (consistent with the placement layer's existing test-out instrument), or (b) accept that the top band's value is *coverage/measurement*, not instruction, and don't pretend to teach them.
Among students *with* a starting MAP, **high-RIT (200+) students complete worst (32% substantial)** while low/mid-RIT complete best (49–56%).
Among MAP'd students, **higher starting ability → lower completion**. This supports **boredom / no-stretch** over frustration
Consistent with §2 (the 130 high-RIT students overlap the older off-grade remediation group placed below their level).
